subject: Throughput regression — FastPay reserved pool contention & exec checkpoint
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@fastpay.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fastpay.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike — FastPay reserved pool (urgent)

Hi Vivek,

We saw a major latency regression this morning across our production endpoints that are served on the Redwood dedicated pool (customer id FP-92). Median p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.6s starting at ~08:50 PST; error rates also climbed for a subset of large-batch requests. Our merchants noticed timeouts during peak checkout windows.

Attached are a short snapshot of our tracing (fastpay_latency_snapshot_1111.json) and server logs with request ids. Ops is continuing to collect traces.

Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood has an immediate mitigation (model fallback, throttle, or burst capacity) we can rely on while we investigate? This is causing conversion loss and we need a clear plan and ETA.

Sara
Sara Miller
Head of Platform Reliability, FastPay
Attachments: fastpay_latency_snapshot_1111.json, fastpay-server-logs-1111.tar.gz

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production latency spike — FastPay reserved pool (urgent)

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. Confirming we received the logs. I'm escalating to SRE and product immediately.

Short plan while we triage:
- Marcus (cc'd) will run a fast root-cause sweep and open a PagerDuty with priority P1; expect an initial triage note within 30 minutes.
- We'll enable an emergency fallback routing policy to a lower-capacity but lower-latency model variant to reduce tail latency for checkout flows (non-invasive, reversible).
- If fallback is insufficient, we will request a 4-hour emergency capacity burst on your Dedicated pool and propose credits for impacted tokens.

Hannah — please coordinate CS comms with FastPay and confirm we can proceed with a temporary downgrade routing if it reduces errors. Laura — need product input on measurable rollback criteria for the fallback.

I'll circle back within 45 minutes with the first technical readout.

— Vivek

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Miller <sara.miller@fastpay.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:52:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production latency spike — FastPay reserved pool (urgent)

Quick technical summary from the triage so far (initial findings):
- Observed symptom: sustained queue depth increase on FastPay's reserved GPU pool starting 08:48 PST. Token processing rate decreased due to increased per-request VK cache misses when many long-context requests arrived simultaneously.
- Root contributor: a canary rollout earlier this morning increased the default request batch window for a subset of endpoints (batch_max_time_ms moved from 8 -> 32ms), which multiplied effective batch sizes during peak — this increased per-batch processing time and triggered backpressure on the autoscaler.
- Autoscaler reaction: conservative scale-up thresholds + a cooldown misconfiguration led to lag in adding nodes. Reserved pool reached 92% utilization and then started queueing; some requests timed out or failed to hit model variants with KV cache primed.

Immediate mitigations implemented (live):
1) Reverted canary batching change for FP's routes (rolled back to 8ms) — live in ~8m.
2) Applied emergency soft-throttling to large-batch traffic (requests with >8k tokens) to limit headroom consumption.
3) Enabled fallback routing to a slightly quantized variant of the same model that has lower tail latency for heavy batches; this reduces quality delta ~1-2% but improves p95 by ~300-400ms in internal tests.

Next steps (need decisions):
- Approve 4hr emergency burst of +2 nodes to the dedicated pool (estimate cost impact and we can offer credits). Can approve now and we'll provision immediately.
- Autoscaler config change (permanent fix): reduce cooldown and add queue-depth aware scale triggers. This needs a config roll in the infra tier and a maintenance window (low-risk but requires sign-off).

Logs and initial graphs uploaded to the incident page: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-78912 (see CPU/queue heatmaps).

Marcus
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Attachments referenced: fastpay-server-logs-1111.tar.gz

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Miller <sara.miller@fastpay.com>, c-suite@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:40:00 -0800
Subject: Exec sync: FastPay throughput regression, recommended commitments and ask

Team — brief recap and exec asks for leadership review:

What happened:
- A canary batching change caused an unexpected multiplication of effective batch sizes during FastPay's peak, causing KV cache churn and sustained queueing on their reserved GPU pool. Autoscaler cooldown settings prevented timely scale-up; reserved pool hit >92% and user-facing p95 increased ~1.4s for checkout flows.

Customer impact:
- Revenue/checkout timeouts reported during a 45m window (major customer; high-risk for renewals/expansion).

Actions taken:
- Canary change rolled back, soft-throttle and model-fallback applied, initial p95 improved ~450ms within 20m of changes.
- Requested emergency +2 nodes for 4 hours; SRE will provision immediately if approved.
- Open action: apply autoscaler config fixes (cooldown+queue triggers) in the infra tier — target for staging test this week and prod rollout next week.

What I am asking leadership to approve now:
1) Emergency dedicated capacity burst: +2 nodes for 4 hours for FastPay (approve billing adjustment / one-time credit).
2) Customer credits: offer FastPay a 30% token credit for the impacted 45m window as a good-faith gesture and to reduce churn risk.
3) Greenlight the infra autoscaler config change and a short maintenance window for rollout next week.

Why these asks: immediate capacity and credits materially reduce churn risk and buy time for the permanent fix. Long-term autoscaler change will prevent recurrence for reserved pools.

If leadership approves, I'll coordinate immediate provisioning and sign-off comms to FastPay. Please reply ASAP; FastPay is monitoring and expects a definitive answer.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
